title: HR Administrator
description:
Job Title: HR Administrator

Location: Sharston, Manchester M22 4 SN

Salary: £27,411.66 per annum

Job type: Full time, Permanent

About us:

Established in 2000, Express Solicitors is an award-winning, no win no fee law firm specialising exclusively in personal injury claims. Headquartered in Manchester, we support clients nationwide across all areas of personal injury, including employers' liability, serious injury, clinical negligence, occupiers' and public liability, road traffic accidents and industrial disease.

We are ranked 64th in The Lawyer UK Top 200, out of more than 10,000 law firms nationwide, and after achieving a 20% year-on-year growth, Express Solicitors are the largest personal injury claimant firm in the UK.

Our commitment to outstanding client care is reflected in our Trustpilot rating of 4.8 (Excellent), placing us among the highest-rated firms in the sector.

About The Role:

We are currently recruiting for a HR Administrator to provide administrative support to our HR Team. This is an exciting opportunity for a talented administrator to join our team and gain valuable HR specialist experience. The right candidate will have the chance to develop their HR career.

Responsibilities:
- Maintain accurate absence records by updating holiday, sickness, medical, and authorised leave information within the HR system.
- Verify that employees enter their data correctly on the HR platform.
- Send a daily absence summary email to all staff.
- Respond to routine staff enquiries in a timely and helpful manner.
- Support the HR team with various projects, such as absenteeism initiatives, company newsletters, HR system improvements, and updates to policies and procedures.
- Coordinate with new starters once an offer is made, including preparing and issuing employment contracts, requesting references, and organising their system setup.
- Deliver induction sessions for new starters.
- Complete checklists for new hires, internal promotions, and leavers to ensure smooth transitions. This includes collaborating with Department Heads and the IT team to share relevant information promptly.
- Ensure personnel files are kept accurate, up-to-date, and well organised.
- Provide general administrative support including filing, scanning, and taking minutes during employee meetings.
- Work with benefits providers, generate ad hoc reports, and liaise with Department Managers as needed.
- Carry out any additional ad hoc duties as required.

Person Specification:
- GCSE Maths and English at Grade 5 or above (or international equivalent).
- Strong administrative and organisational skills.
- Good numerical ability.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office, especially Excel, Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint.
- Flexible and able to prioritise tasks effectively in a dynamic environment.
- Resilient and capable of working under pressure.
- Willing and eager to learn.
- Excellent understanding of confidentiality, with the ability to handle sensitive information discreetly.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Confident and professional telephone manner.
- High level of accuracy and strong attention to detail.
- Demonstrated ability to coordinate and manage information effectively.
- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced work environment.
- Previous HR administration experience and an understanding of UK employment law are desirable but not essential.
- A relevant HR qualification is an advantage.

Salary & Hours:
- Salary of £27,411.66 based on 39.5 hours
- Our standard working hours are 8:30am to 5:30pm Monday-Thursday and 8:30am to 5pm Friday.

Benefits:
- Hybrid Working - 3/2 hybrid working pattern after probation.
- 23 Days Holiday - Rising to 26 days, plus bank/public holidays.
- Extra Holidays - 3 holiday buy backs and an extra day for your birthday after service length requirement.
- Looking After Your Health - Private medical insurance available after 2 years' service, annual flu jab and Employee Assistance Programme.
- Looking After Your Well-being - 24/7 onsite Gym, Netball/Football team, 10km Manchester team and more.
- Work Life / Balance - Active social committee with generous departmental and firm-wide social budget.

Recruitment Process:

Interviews will be conducted by MS Teams and will include scenario-based questioning.

Our employees are our most important asset, we rate skill and ability above all else and our recruitment policy encourages applications from all.

Please click APPLY to be redirected to our website to complete your application.

Candidates with the relevant experience or job titles of; HR Assistant, Human Resources Assistant, Human Resources Executive, HR Executive, Human Resources Administrator, HR Advisor, Human Resources Advisor, HR Generalist, Human Resources Admin, HR Officer, HR Admin may also be considered for this role.

title: Commercial Litigation Paralegal
description:
Job Title: Commercial Litigation Paralegal
Location: Manchester City Centre
Salary: £24,000 to £27,000 per annum
Contract: Full or Part Time, Permanent

Overview:

Our client is a leading claims management law firm, specialising in a broad range of commercial and civil litigation matters. The firm has built a strong reputation for delivering successful outcomes for its clients while maintaining a friendly yet professional working environment.

Based in modern offices in the heart of Manchester City Centre, the firm offers an excellent opportunity for a Litigation Paralegal to join a well-established and forward-thinking practice. The successful candidate will work alongside experienced solicitors and team leaders, gaining exposure to high-quality litigation work and benefiting from clear opportunities for long-term development.

Position:

The Litigation Paralegal will provide comprehensive legal and administrative support to solicitors and team leaders across a varied litigation caseload. The role involves assisting with day-to-day case management, conducting legal research and pre-claim investigations, and providing initial assessments of new cases.

You will be responsible for preparing, editing, and proofreading a wide range of legal documents, including pleadings, trial bundles, and instructions to counsel. The position also requires drafting professional correspondence for clients and third parties, handling enquiries from clients, opposing counsel, and other stakeholders via phone, email, and in person, and maintaining accurate case files and CRM records.

The role includes coordinating court schedules, managing the administrative aspects of assigned claims, and supporting settlement discussions, mediations, and other alternative dispute resolution processes between businesses and insurers. You may also accompany counsel to court hearings and trials, assisting with case preparation and documentation.

In addition, you will support effective internal collaboration by undertaking general administrative duties that help ensure smooth communication across departments.

Key Details:

This Litigation Paralegal position is offered on a full or part-time, permanent basis and is based in Manchester City Centre. The salary on offer ranges from £24,000 to £27,000 per annum, depending on experience.

The successful candidate will join a firm that provides a competitive benefits package, including 25 days' annual leave plus bank holidays, a pension scheme, company social events, and structured training and development. A clear career development pathway is also in place, making this an excellent opportunity for a Litigation Paralegal seeking long-term progression.

Introducing CRA Consulting:

CRA Consulting are a specialist legal recruiter operating across the UK. We work in partnership with reputable law firms with local, regional, national, and international presence, recruiting at all levels from board, director, and partnership level through to support staff.

How to Apply:

If this Litigation Paralegal opportunity is of interest, please click the apply button to submit your application. Alternatively, for a confidential discussion about the role, you can contact Umar Tawil at CRA Consulting, who is managing this vacancy.

title: Children Law Paralegal - Manchester
description:
Role: Children Paralegal

Duncan Lewis Solicitors is seeking a motivated and talented Child Care Paralegal to join our highly regarded Child Care Department. This is an excellent opportunity to develop your career with one of the UK's leading law firms, recognised by The Legal 500 and Chambers & Partners as a top-tier practice and awarded Law Firm of the Year at both the 2024 LexisNexis Awards and the 2023 Modern Law Awards.

Founded in 1998 and headquartered in the City of London, Duncan Lewis Solicitors is a national, award-winning, paperless law firm with over 500 professionals nationwide. Our ethos is simple: "We give people a voice."

Our highly specialised Child Care Department is recognised by The Legal 500 as "an extremely knowledgeable and hugely capable child care team" and is ranked for its expertise across all aspects of child care law. The team represents children, parents, guardians and family members in a broad range of matters, including care proceedings, adoption, surrogacy, co-parenting arrangements and international child issues. The department is distinguished by its exceptional accreditations, with many team members holding Law Society Children Panel membership and membership of the Association of Lawyers for Children, and Duncan Lewis being one of the few firms in the UK on the Lord Chancellor's International Child Abduction and Contact Unit (ICACU) referral list.

Joining Duncan Lewis means becoming part of a diverse, supportive and forward-thinking organisation where you will have the opportunity to work alongside highly regarded specialists on complex and often high-profile cases that make a real difference to children and families.

Duties and responsibilities

As a Children Law Paralegal, you will play a key role in supporting clients across a broad range of child care matters, assisting children, parents, guardians and family members through complex and often sensitive proceedings while helping to achieve the best possible outcomes for those involved.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Report directly to Department Director
- Professional pro-active approach, strong client care skills and a sensitive and sympathetic understanding of clients' needs
- Assisting with casework including dealing with a range of public and private children cases including child abduction; child protection issues; special guardianship and adoption matters as well as undertaking your own advocacy
- Attending clients, taking instructions and preparing cases
- Dealing with correspondence
- Maintaining accurate time costing procedures
- Implementing any recommendations made by your supervisor following monthly file reviews ensuring that these are dealt with promptly
- Ensuring compliance with file management

Experience and qualifications

The successful candidate will demonstrate a genuine interest in Children Law and a commitment to delivering exceptional client service.

Essential requirements include:
- A strong academic background with a Law degree
- Demonstrate passion and experience in a broad range of publicly funded Child Care Law
- Legal experience as a Child Care Paralegal/Advisor
- Clear understanding and application of Children Laws
- Excellent legal research, drafting and analytical skills.
- Strong organisational and time management abilities.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- Professional, motivated and client-focused approach.
- Business acumen and the ability to market the Company
- Excellent communications skills to work effectively with all types of people
- Excellent analytical and organisational skills and ability to use own initiative but know when to seek guidance
- Strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office and document management systems.

Benefits

We offer a competitive salary and a comprehensive range of benefits designed to support your professional development, wellbeing, and work-life balance, including:
- Competitive salary with structured pay review process
- Company pension scheme
- 22 days annual leave, increasing with length of service
- Additional birthday leave
- Occupational sick pay
- Payment of practising certificate and relevant professional membership fees
- Access to extensive e-library resources and training webinars
- Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) and wellbeing support
- Employee referral scheme
- Eye care vouchers
- Enhanced family-friendly benefits
- DBS checks paid by the Company
- Flexible and hybrid working options, including part-time arrangements where appropriate
- Support for solicitor qualification and SQE1 examinations
- Clear career progression opportunities
- Support for industry recognition, awards, and professional profile development
- Company Medical Cash Plan

Subject to eligibility and Company policy.

Company culture

At Duncan Lewis Solicitors, we are passionate about creating an environment where talented professionals can thrive. We are proud of our diverse and inclusive workforce and are committed to providing equal opportunities for all employees.

Our long-standing Investors in People Gold Standard accreditation reflects our commitment to employee development, while our Lexcel, Cyber Essentials Plus and ISO 27001 certifications demonstrate our dedication to excellence, innovation and security.

We invest heavily in the growth of our people through ongoing training, mentoring, clear progression pathways and opportunities to gain industry recognition. Whether you are looking to deepen your expertise, develop leadership skills or advance your career within a nationally recognised law firm, Duncan Lewis provides the platform to help you succeed.

Join a firm where your expertise is valued, your development is supported, and your work makes a genuine difference to the lives of clients across the UK.

title: Asset Servicing Administrator (12 Month Fixed-Term Contract)
description:
Job Description

We are recruiting an Asset Servicing Administrator to join our Corporate Actions Processing team. You'll be responsible for the accurate and timely processing of corporate action events across multiple markets and instruments, working alongside a team of administrators to deliver an excellent service to our customers.

Asset Servicing sits within our Custody function and is made up of three teams: Event Capture, Dividends Processing and Corporate Actions Processing. We're looking for a detail-oriented individual with strong analytical skills to ensure all corporate action events are processed accurately. In this role you'll manage your own workload throughout the day, work closely with colleagues to make sure the team's work is completed, and play a key part in safeguarding client assets and minimising operational risk within a regulated environment

What does the job involve?
- Monitor, capture and process mandatory and voluntary corporate action events
- Interpret and validate information received from custodians, vendors and market announcements
- Ensure entitlements are accurately reflected in client accounts and systems
- Instructing counterparties / custodians
- Reconciling positions at different stages through the event
- Investigate and resolve reconciliation breaks promptly, escalating unresolved items to management
- Processing events to customer accounts
- Notifying customers when events are completed
- Liaise with custodians, brokers and internal teams to resolve discrepancies
- Ensuring that we are adhering with all compliance policies including AML, CASS, and breach reporting

What you'll have:
- Knowledge of the corporate action lifecycle, from announcement to settlement
- Good knowledge of financial instruments, including equities, bonds and funds
- Ability to work in high pressure deadline driven environments
- Excellent attention to detail and a risk-aware mindset
- Strong problem-solving and analytical skills
- A highly organised and methodical approach to work
- Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain complex issues clearly
- The ability to work independently and under pressure to meet tight deadlines
- A collaborative team player who is willing to share knowledge
- Advanced excel skills

Credit Hire Claims Handler
Location: Manchester City Centre (Office-based during probation)
Working Hours: 40 hours per week
Salary: £32,000 + 10% Discretionary Bonus

IPS Group is working with an innovative and fast-growing InsurTech that is continuing to expand its UK claims operation. Due to ongoing growth, they are looking to appoint a Credit Hire Claims Handler to join their newly established claims team in Manchester.
This is a great opportunity to join the business at an exciting stage of its journey. As one of the early hires within the claims function, you'll have the chance to make a real impact, contribute to the development of processes and customer outcomes, and position yourself for future progression as the team continues to grow.

The Role
You will manage your own caseload of third-party Credit Hire claims from instruction through to settlement or litigation. Working closely with clients, claimants, insurers and third parties, you'll be responsible for progressing claims efficiently while delivering positive outcomes throughout the claims journey. The role will involve reviewing liability, handling quantum disputes, assessing supporting evidence and negotiating settlements. You'll also review payment packs, utilise Verify as part of the claims process and identify any potentially fraudulent activity or underwriting concerns where appropriate.
As the UK operation continues to grow, you'll play an important role in helping shape processes and delivering an excellent customer experience.

Key Responsibilities Include:
- Managing a caseload of third-party Credit Hire claims from instruction through to settlement or litigation
- Reviewing liability and handling quantum disputes
- Liaising with clients, claimants, insurers and third parties to progress claims efficiently
- Reviewing payment packs and utilising Verify within the claims process
- Negotiating settlements and achieving commercially focused outcomes
- Maintaining accurate claim records, reserves and payments
- Delivering excellent levels of customer service throughout the claims lifecycle

About You:
You'll have previous Credit Hire claims experience and be confident managing your own caseload with minimal supervision. Ideally, you'll have at least two years' experience handling motor-related Credit Hire claims from inception through to settlement.
You will also have:
- A strong understanding of UK motor insurance principles and claims processes
- Knowledge of liability assessment, indemnity and quantum calculations
- The ability to investigate claims, review evidence and make sound decisions
- A proactive approach and the ability to work effectively within a fast-paced environment

What's in it for You?
Alongside a competitive salary, you'll benefit from private medical cover, life insurance, pension support and overtime enhancements where applicable. The role is hybrid following probation, with the opportunity to have 1 day working from home.

This is also a rare opportunity to join a newly established claims function within a growing InsurTech business. As one of the first members of the team, you'll have genuine opportunities to develop your career as the operation expands, whilst helping to shape the future success of the team.

description: We have a vacancy for Medical Receptionist/Administrators to join our friendly reception team. We are a small but high-performing practice. The post is for 30 hours per week. We pay living wage, adjusted for experience and age. Essential: Good computer skills and previous customer-facing employment experience. Preferrable: Experience of working in a busy healthcare setting and knowledge of clinical systems, e.g. EMIS Web and Docman. Answering phones and booking and cancelling appointments Booking patients in on arrival or directing patients to the check-in kiosk Actioning repeat prescription requests and prescription enquiries Ensuring all referral PNs are done by end of working day Actioning patient enquiries and patient notes on EMISWeb Job Description Reception Cherry Medical Practice In this post you will be expected to perform and be competent in the following tasks as part of your daily duties. title: Experienced Medical Receptionist
description: We are looking to recruit a Full time Experienced Receptionist/Administrator to join our team at New Islington Medical Practice. This is an essential role providing a welcoming and professional service to our patients and staff of the practice. The vacancy is for 37.5hrs however we will consider flexible working and compressed hours during the recruitment process. You will be expected to undertake front-desk responsibilities, and be able to assist patients both on the phone and using our online consultation forms. Your duties will involve the day to day administrative tasks of the practice including but not limited to secretarial work and in depth use of the clinical systems. To be successful in our team, we are looking for someone who is dynamic in their approach and able to balance multiple tasks. We pride ourselves on our compassionate nature with our patients, and this is an essential characteristic that we are looking for. Flexibility is a must, as we work on a shift basis with the normal opening hours of 8am to 6.30pm. We would require any successful candidate to be able to cover other shifts outside their regular pattern to assist with holiday cover. There is also the option of enhanced pay for hours outside of this window for our extended hours service. Previous experience is preferred, however it is not essential as full training will be provided to the successful candidate. Reception duties include the following: (this list is not exhaustive) Booking telephone appointments through inbound calls. Calling and messaging patients with regards to their care needs - managing appointments and health campaigns and working with priorities set by the management team. Updating patient records - Accurate information and full documentation of actions. Processing online consultation forms. General administrative tasks. Ability to differentiate differing needs of a wide population and adjust processes and protocols to suit the patient need. Safeguarding vulnerable patients - full training provided as first point of contact to recognise and flag safeguarding concerns.

title: Medical Receptionist / Administrator
description: Medical Receptionist Join Our Friendly GP Practice We are looking for an experienced, friendly and reliable Medical Receptionist to join our busy GP practice. This is a varied and demanding role where you will be the first point of contact for our patients. You will need to be confident, calm and compassionate, with the ability to communicate effectively with patients who may sometimes be upset, frustrated or challenging. The successful candidate will understand that GP reception is a busy and sometimes challenging environment . You will need to be able to remain calm when the phones are ringing, the waiting room is busy and patients are frustrated, while continuing to provide a professional and compassionate service. You will also need to be comfortable maintaining boundaries and following practice policies, even when dealing with difficult conversations. Previous experience within general practice and knowledge of EMIS would be highly desirable. Essential working pattern You must be available to work Monday: 1:00pm 6:30pm Friday: 8:00am 6:30pm Additional hours may be available depending on the needs of the practice. Please do not apply if you are unable to commit to these days and hours. The role Your responsibilities will include: Welcoming patients and visitors and providing a professional and friendly first point of contact Answering a busy telephone line and dealing with patient enquiries Booking, cancelling and rearranging appointments Using EMIS to access and update patient records and manage appointments Processing prescription requests and other administrative enquiries Dealing appropriately and sensitively with confidential and sometimes complex information Liaising with GPs, nurses, pharmacists and the wider practice team Maintain accurate patient records Follow practice procedures relating to confidentiality, safeguarding and information governance Dealing professionally with difficult or challenging patients and situations Supporting colleagues and contributing to the smooth running of the practice We are a friendly practice with a 4088 patients list size. The clinical team is 2 GP, ANP, Practice Nurse, Nurse associate, 2 prescribing pharmacists, 2 long term locums, practice manager, SAS manager and admin / reception team. To provide a professional, efficient and welcoming reception service to patients and visitors, ensuring that patients receive appropriate assistance and are directed to the most suitable healthcare professional or service. The post holder will work as part of the wider practice team and will contribute to the effective day-to-day running of the reception and administrative functions of the practice. The role requires excellent communication skills, a calm and professional approach and the ability to deal sensitively and appropriately with patients who may be distressed, frustrated or challenging. Provide a friendly, professional and welcoming service to all patients and visitors. Act as the first point of contact for patients contacting the practice by telephone, face-to-face or through other communication channels. Answer telephone calls promptly and professionally, dealing with enquiries appropriately. Book, cancel and rearrange appointments using EMIS Web . Ensure patients are directed to the most appropriate clinician, service or healthcare provider in accordance with practice procedures. Provide patients with appropriate information regarding appointments, services and practice procedures. Deal appropriately with urgent requests and escalate concerns to the appropriate member of the clinical or management team. Assist patients who may have additional needs, including those who are elderly, vulnerable or require additional support. Accurately access and update patient records using EMIS Web. Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient information in accordance with practice procedures. Process prescription requests in line with practice policy. Process incoming and outgoing correspondence as required. Undertake administrative tasks associated with patient care and the smooth running of the practice. Complete tasks accurately and within required timescales. Maintain a good working knowledge of practice systems and procedures. Communicate clearly, professionally and courteously with patients, relatives, carers and colleagues. Remain calm and professional when dealing with difficult, distressed or angry patients. Use appropriate communication and de-escalation techniques when managing challenging situations. Maintain appropriate professional boundaries while remaining compassionate and helpful. Escalate aggressive, threatening or inappropriate behaviour in accordance with practice procedures. Report any concerns regarding patient safety, safeguarding or behaviour to the appropriate member of staff. Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, pharmacists, healthcare professionals, administrative staff and management. Support colleagues during busy periods and assist with maintaining an effective reception service. Attend team meetings and training sessions as required. Communicate relevant information effectively to colleagues. Be flexible and willing to undertake additional duties within the scope of the role when required. Maintain strict patient confidentiality at all times. Comply with GDPR, UK data protection legislation and practice information governance policies. Ensure patient information is only accessed and shared appropriately. Maintain confidentiality when dealing with patients both within and outside the practice. Follow practice policies relating to information security and the use of clinical systems. Maintain an awareness of safeguarding responsibilities within general practice. Recognise and appropriately escalate concerns relating to children, young people and vulnerable adults. Follow the practice safeguarding policies and procedures. Complete mandatory safeguarding training as required. Comply with practice health and safety policies. Report accidents, incidents, hazards and concerns appropriately. Maintain a clean, safe and professional reception environment. Follow infection prevention and control procedures. Complete mandatory training relevant to the role.
